messages.author: 367a410990c0de10
messages.subject: Creating New Shiny Output Binding
parts:
I have been trying to create a new Shiny output binding following the example here:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/tree/master/054-nvd3-line-chart-output

I am at a point where the app runs without any fatal errors, no JavaScript errors in the inspector, but a considerable number of CSS warnings and errors coming from the bootstrap and leaflet stylesheets I'm using from CDN. The result is the Shiny UI rendering correctly, but no output from the custom Shiny output binding.

I would appreciate anyone with more HTML/CSS/JavaScript experience to take a look to see if the culprit can be identified either in the way I am assigning/calling it or in the JavaScript itself. Here is a fully reproducible Git repo:

https://github.com/McClellandKemp/leaflet_heatmap

For clarity I have produced a toy example of the desired output, also in the repo with permalink:

https://github.com/McClellandKemp/leaflet_heatmap/blob/773770ad06cb6a03dd1e74d41d714a09f16b5800/www/goal_result.html

Thanks very much in advance!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Creating New Shiny Output Binding
parts:
The Leaflet R package will soon support heatmaps, there's been a pull request sitting open for many months but I haven't looked at Leaflet in quite a while. I'm hoping to spend some time on this in the next 8 weeks and heatmap is near the top of the list in terms of priority.

In the meantime you can use the approach sketched out in this example:
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/c084a59717f18e947a17955007dc5f92#file-leaflet-heat-r

Note: you'll need to devtools::install_github("ramnathv/htmlwidgets") for this to work.

messages.subject: Re: Creating New Shiny Output Binding
parts:
Thanks for the quick response!

The reason I moved away from the Leaflet R package (amazing though it is!) was that it was my understanding that I couldn't get away from the EPSG:3857 projection system leaflet expects -- my goal was to set a ratio of 1:1 pixel to internal lat/lon and zoom a digital image.

Is there a way to set a custom projection in your package that I haven't uncovered?

If not would you mind taking a quick look at the example I have? The custom binding looks to be an extremely powerful concept that I'd like to at least have a base understanding of.
